Three-Time Asian Para Games Gold Medallist Neeraj Yadav Passes Away at 42

Tragic Loss for Indian Para-Athletics

Indian para-athletics is mourning the death of three-time Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav, who allegedly died by suicide at his flat on Tuesday night. According to reports, the 42-year-old athlete, who competed in the F55 category, is suspected to have consumed poison. A postmortem examination was underway at Delhi's GTB Hospital on Wednesday. Paralympic champion Sumit Antil and fellow para-athlete Vipin Kasana were present at the hospital following the incident.

India's chief para-athletics coach, S Satyanarayana, confirmed the tragic news, stating he had been informed that Yadav consumed poison at his residence. The precise circumstances surrounding his death have not yet been officially established by authorities.

Sporting Career and Achievements

Diagnosed with post-polio residual paralysis at the age of seven, Yadav pursued sports despite his physical challenges. He initially played wheelchair tennis from 2005 to 2012 before transitioning to para-athletics. His breakthrough arrived at the 2015 Delhi State Athletics Meet, where he secured gold medals in the shot put, javelin, and discus events.

On the international stage, Yadav made a significant impact at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, claiming gold in the men's F55 javelin throw with an Asian-record distance of 29.84 metres. He followed this success with two additional gold medals at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Para Games, winning both the javelin and discus events to bring his career tally to three continental titles.

However, his career faced a setback due to an anti-doping case. The National Anti-Doping Agency provisionally suspended Yadav after an out-of-competition sample collected in Bengaluru in October 2023 tested positive for stanozolol, an anabolic steroid. He subsequently sought DNA testing of his sample through the disciplinary process.

Confirmed Facts Versus Unknowns

  • Confirmed: Neeraj Yadav passed away at the age of 42 on Tuesday night; the cause of death is suspected to be poisoning; a postmortem examination was scheduled at GTB Hospital; he was a decorated athlete with three Asian Para Games gold medals; and he was serving a provisional doping suspension.
  • Unknown: The exact sequence of events leading up to the incident and the precise psychological factors influencing his final actions remain unconfirmed by formal investigations.
